events.headline: Russia launched a mixed missile/drone barrage (~140 drones) on Ukraine overnight Oct 25-26 while rejecting ceasefire terms Zelensky proposed; Ukraine struck Russian munitions plants in Yelets and at the Energiya facility, keeping the war's intensity elevated with no near-term resolution

Yemen's Houthis struck Saudi Aramco facilities near Riyadh and Khurais with missiles and drones in early October, part of a broader pattern of Mideast supply-chain attacks that, combined with the ongoing US-Iran conflict and new Russia oil-sanctions risk, has pushed Brent crude to six-month highs (~$114-116/bbl)

Oil settled near six-month highs Monday (Brent $115.81, WTI $101.76) as traders weigh Mideast attack risk and looming Russia oil sanctions against hopes of Ukraine de-escalation; US SPR stocks fell to their lowest level since 1982

Wall Street banks and Blackstone lined up $63B to finance Broadcom AI chips/networking gear for Anthropic, and Meta raised its planned equity offering to $97.5B with Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom pledging up to $5B combined; chip stocks rallied broadly (Nvidia +2.4%, AMD +2.8%, Micron +3.0%, Broadcom +2.3%) on renewed AI-buildout optimism following Anthropic's IPO filing

China's temporary suspension of rare-earth and lithium-battery-material export controls is set to expire November 10, 2026 with no extension announced yet, leaving chip and battery supply chains exposed to renewed curbs

The Fed's Oct 27-28 FOMC meeting is widely expected to hold the benchmark rate at 3.75%-4.00% (CME FedWatch ~83-91% odds of a hold; a Reuters poll found 94/100 economists expect a hold), tempering near-term rate-hike risk
